title: Invertibility and base change of the Kummer-normalized two-component maps
statement: Under the hypotheses and coefficient conventions of [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-data], fix a normalized twist transport and a family of projective-line Chern arrows satisfying the actual Kummer specification [def-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-kummer-class]. The map with components the shifted twisted unit and the adjoint Chern arrow is an isomorphism for every Noetherian base. For every map of such bases its square with the canonical exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], normalized shifted-line comparison and ordered sum comparison commutes. This statement asserts neither a trace adjunction nor its triangular identities.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z/N$. The general standard-chart statement [lem-weil-pbc-projective-space-standard-charts](a),(c), specialized to the two coordinates, supplies the covering charts $\operatorname{Spec}B[t]$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B[s]$ over every affine open $\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq S$, with $t=x_1/x_0$, $s=x_0/x_1$. Their product charts are $\operatorname{Spec}B[t,u]$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra]: $B[t]\otimes_B B[u]\cong B[t,u]$ by multiplication of monomials. The same chart statement applies to either $p_a$ over base $P$. The maps $q,p_a$ are proper by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper], hence finite type and quasi-compact; [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] makes their sources locally Noetherian, and quasi-compactness gives Noetherian sources. Properness makes $q$ separated, so its diagonal is closed and therefore proper of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper]. Thus [lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] applies to $q,p_a,\Delta$ with either finite ring $R$ or $A$, on the entire derived categories. Use throughout its specified ordered, symmetry-conjugated projection map. All proper exchanges are isomorphisms by [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring]. The twists are flat rank-one sheaves by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], with canonical pullbacks by [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback].

source.place: Hypotheses for the diagonal construction and proper exchange

proof.text: For the geometric fibre over an algebraically closed field, apply the genus-zero projective-line theorem and proper-curve cohomology. A primitive root transports the constant Z/N computation to mu_N. The genus is zero, so H1 is the zero function group on Fin 0; H0 and H2 are Z/N and all higher groups vanish. This part is proved in ordinaryFiniteP1_geometric_cohomology. To normalize the actual arrow, use the existing adopted-library degree trace sheafHTwoTrace: the second Kummer boundary has kernel N Pic and is onto, and divisibility of Pic0 makes this trace bijective. It sends a line bundle's boundary to its degree modulo N. The two-chart coherent cohomology of O(d), d>=0, gives h0=d+1 and h1=0; the dimension-vanishing theorem gives chi=d+1. Since the unit is O(0), the definition of degree gives deg O(1)=2-1=1. Thus the trace sends its actual Kummer boundary to one, as proved in ordinaryFiniteP1_geometric_kummer_normalization. The shifted twisted unit is the identity on H0. Use proper exchange to identify geometric stalks of the relative pushforward with these fibre groups. Exact conservative geometric stalks and the unbounded cohomology criterion then show that the specified two-component map is invertible over Z/N.

Apply $e_S^*=A_S\otimes_R^L-$ to $b_{q,R}$. Use [lem-asd-proper-finite-coefficient-extension] at $f=q$, $R=\mathbf Z/N\to A$, and $L=\mu_{N,P}[2]$. Its $A$-linear isomorphism identifies the resulting target with $Rq_{*,A}e_P^*(\mu_{N,P}[2])$. By [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], $\mu_N$ is $R$-flat, so this is $Rq_{*,A}A_P(1)[2]$, even for nonflat $A$. The source is $A_S(1)[2]\oplus A_S$. The second component is $h$ by its scalar-extension definition. For the first component, transpose under $q_A^{-1}\dashv Rq_{*,A}$: the normalization of the comparison gives scalar extension of $\varepsilon_R q_R^{-1}(\text{unit}_R)=1$, so the component is the shifted twisted $A$-unit. Thus the resulting arrow is exactly $b_q$. Derived scalar extension preserves the isomorphism $b_{q,R}$, and the comparison is an isomorphism; hence $b_q$ is an isomorphism.

Under any change of Noetherian base, the infinity divisor remains Cartier: its chart equation is a polynomial variable. Its dual ideal pulls back to O(1). Apply [lem-asd-ordinary-supported-kummer] and [lem-amb-kummer-any-base] to identify the pulled-back Kummer class. The comparison [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-class-comparison] identifies its derived representative. The unit/exchange equation follows by expanding the mate [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] and cancelling the adjunction triangle. The normalized twist transport and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-exchange-tensor-coherence] identify the two ordered components. Their biproduct desc therefore gives the stated commuting square.
